referents.why: 'my' on the soul: first person common singular, and the psalm's own voice is the only first-person candidate.
'me' as object of the yiqtol in cl1: first person singular; the psalm does not quote another speaker here, so it is the psalm's own voice.
'his' on the name: third masculine singular possessor. The only masculine singular divine candidate is the LORD of the preceding verse, whose name the phrase invokes.
implied subject of the yiqtol in cl0, third masculine singular. The shepherd sentence of 23:1 names the LORD as subject and the implied He continues it.
referents.category: implied subject of a continuing divine action

referents.why: implied subject of the yiqtol in cl1, third masculine singular, the same agent as the clause before it; the LORD is the only agreeing candidate.
referents.category: implied subject of a continuing divine action

groups.why: Two clauses in a row joined by no conjunction, each with a yiqtol whose subject is implied and is the same LORD. This is the acts pattern rather than a command, so it is a group of one agent's acts, not an imperative.
groups.category: one agent's clauses in a row without conjunction

none_fit.where: cl1, 'for the sake of his name' (לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ)
none_fit.what: a nominal purpose phrase inside the clause, not a clause; the purpose link takes clause-to-clause sources, so no link is added.
